decisionsTitle: The club's logo as a pale watermark at the foot of the volunteers' badges — «Logo-ul clubului jos, ca filigran»
decisionsSection: **The owner, 2026-11-17, four days before Saturday's race (2026-11-21), designing the volunteers' badges:** «vreau ca la voluntari să pot pune logo-ul clubului în footer, dar transparent». Asked how, he chose: **a large, pale watermark of the club's logo at the bottom of the badge — the name written in marker reads over it — with a choice of how visible it is: a little, medium, or well**. Amends §764 (what a badge prints) and the writing area of §776. **Decision.** - **One key in the badge's design, `footerLogo`:** `off`, `faint`, `medium`, `strong` — «Fără», «Puțin vizibil», «Mediu», «Bine vizibil». `off` by default and for every design saved before the choice, read so by the one forgiving reader (`readBadgeDesign`), never refused; a level no one knows, or a value of the wrong type (a file made by hand, a later release's level), reads `off` too and the designer says so beside its section, as §783's choice of badge does. The form: a native select «Logo-ul clubului jos, ca filigran» in «Locul pentru nume», under «O linie subțire pentru nume», with one help line — «Logo-ul clubului mare și palid în partea de jos a ecusonului. Numele scris cu markerul se citește peste el.» — and the section's closed line naming the level when one is chosen. The preview follows the unsaved choice: the select is one of the designer's controls and the preview's address carries the key. A word that is none of the four is refused, naming the box; a form from before the select posts none, which is `off`. Saved and audited as every key of the design is (`event.badge_design_changed`, the key named), and carried by the event's file under `badges.design.footerLogo` — the import's diff naming it — and by a copy of the event. - **What is drawn.** With a level chosen, every badge of the event — a role's, a role's under a category, «fără rol» and the one badge for everyone — draws the club's lockup (`club/club.json`'s `logo.lockup`) in its own colours: on the sheet the raster the header and the bib's member mark already draw (`src/theme/pdf/logo.png`), in the picture the same file. It stands in the writing area's lower part: from the foot of «Nume:»'s line (one line at the largest size «Nume:» and the marker's label are set at) down to the writing area's foot less half the pad — centred across the badge, as large as that room allows at the lockup's own proportion (`LOGO_RATIO`), never wider than two thirds of the badge, standing on the room's foot. Measured: 21.7 × 8.9 mm on the default 90 × 35 mm strip (a quarter of its width), 25.2 × 10.4 mm on 100 × 40 mm, 18.2 × 7.5 mm on the smallest badge the designer accepts, 60 × 30 mm (15.7 × 6.5 mm there with the telephone), 14.3 × 5.9 mm on the default strip when the free-text line and the telephone take the writing area down to its 10 mm; on a tall badge it reaches two thirds of the width (40 mm on 60 × 100 mm). - **The three levels:** `faint` 0.12, `medium` 0.22, `strong` 0.35 — the values asked for, kept after looking at the PDF sheet and the picture at each level: «Puțin vizibil» is a light tint that is still the logo, «Bine vizibil» is plainly the club's blue, and a marker's black reads first over each. - **Drawn first in the writing area** — after the role's band and the free-text line, before «Nume:» — so «Nume:», the line for the name and the marker's divider, label and line are drawn over it, never under. No ground of its own: the raster's white falls on the white writing area at the same opacity, so only the logo shows. On the sheet the opacity is set in a graphics state of its own (`save`, `opacity`, `restore`), so nothing else is drawn pale; in the picture it is the ``'s own `opacity`. - **It takes no height.** No row moves and no line moves: `badgeRows`, every line of the layout and the save's fit check (`badgeSizeRefusal`, `BADGE_SIZE_TOO_SMALL`) are what they were, so a design that fits today fits with the logo and a size refused today is refused alike. Tested at every width step of 10 mm and every whole height the bounds allow, with every row ticked: the box inside the writing area under «Nume:», over no band and no row, the rest of the layout identical; and at the smallest sizes accepted (60 × 30 mm, and 60 × 34 mm with the free-text line and the telephone). - **One source.** The box and the opacity are computed once, by `badgeFooterLogoBox` in `badge-geometry.ts`, which `badgeLayout` puts in the layout both renderers draw: the sheet (`badges-pdf.ts`), the picture (`badge-image.tsx`, through the preview route) and so the print panel's pictures cannot disagree — the tests read the PDF's call and the picture's markup back into the same box and opacity. `BADGE_DRAWING_VERSION` is 3, so every picture's address changes. - **Off draws as before, byte for byte.** While `off` the layout has no new key, the picture no new element and the sheet no new call: the drawing kept by the previous change (`tests/unit/volunteers/badge-type-unchanged.test.ts` and its snapshot) holds unchanged, now also for the key chosen `off` and for a design stored before it. A badge still carries no person (§764): the watermark is the club's own file, the same on every badge. **Not done (each its own change, when asked).** Another picture than the club's logo (a sponsor's, the event's); any change to the logo in the header; a separate footer band; a coloured or grey version of the logo; the race numbers (bibs); a choice of where the watermark stands or how large it is; a level per role. **Refused.** A band of its own at the badge's foot: it would take height from the writing area, the part a badge is for, and turn sizes accepted today into refusals. Rising beside «Nume:» to be larger: the label stays clean and the logo stands where the name is written — the room under «Nume:» is what decides its size. A new raster with transparency: the header's own file on the white writing area shows only the logo, and an alpha picture in a PDF composites badly on some viewers and printers (§174's reason for flattening the rasters).
changelogLine: - **The club's logo as a watermark on the volunteers' badges** — «Logo-ul clubului jos, ca filigran» in the badge designer puts the club's logo, large and pale, at the bottom of every badge under «Nume:», «Puțin vizibil», «Mediu» or «Bine vizibil»; the name written in marker reads over it, the preview shows it before the save, and nothing else on the badge moves. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given «Cum arată ecusonul», then «Locul pentru nume» has «Logo-ul clubului jos, ca filigran» — a native select of «Fără», «Puțin vizibil», «Mediu» and «Bine vizibil» with one help line, its section's closed line naming the level chosen — and the preview follows the choice before the save; «Salvează ecusonul» keeps it in `events.badge_design` as `footerLogo` (`off`, `faint`, `medium`, `strong`) and audits the key changed; a word that is none of the four is refused naming the box with every box kept; a design stored, or an event file made, before the choice reads `off`, and a stored level no one knows reads `off` and is named beside the section — never a throw; the key travels in the event's file under `badges.design`, the diff naming it, and in a copy of the event (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a badge design with a level chosen, then every badge of the event — a role's, a badge «fără rol» and the one badge for everyone — draws the club's lockup once, in its own colours and with no ground of its own, centred across the badge in the writing area's lower part, under «Nume:»'s line and above the writing area's foot, never wider than two thirds of the badge, at the level's opacity (0.12, 0.22, 0.35), first in the writing area so that «Nume:», the lines and the marker's area are drawn over it, and never over the header, the role's band, the free-text line or the telephone's row; the PDF sheet, the picture and the print panel's pictures draw the same box at the same opacity; no row moves, and at every size the designer accepts the save answers the size as it does without the logo (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a badge design with `footerLogo` off — chosen, or absent from a design stored before the choice — then every badge prints exactly what it printed before: the same layout, the same picture and the same calls to the PDF (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the club's logo as a pale watermark at the foot of the volunteers' badges («Logo-ul clubului jos, ca filigran»)
